summary.headline: Aequs Q1 FY27 revenue rose 55% YoY to INR3,955 million, while operational EBITDA rose about 3.5x QoQ to INR148 million.
summary.overview: Revenue from operations grew 55% YoY and 8% QoQ to INR3,955 million, led by aerospace (+40% YoY) and consumer (+190% YoY). Reported EBITDA fell QoQ to INR215 million because other income dropped from INR279 million to INR67 million, but operational EBITDA (excluding other income) rose from INR42 million to INR148 million. Consumer EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million QoQ to INR361 million. PAT loss was INR532 million, and the aerospace order book crossed USD1 billion after Farnborough wins including an A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 45-50% revenue growth and doubled operational EBITDA, with consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27.

segments.name: Aerospace
segments.commentary: Revenue INR3,222 million (+40% YoY, +6% QoQ) with segment EBITDA INR731 million (about 23% margin). Order book USD1,004 million, up 13% QoQ from USD889 million; 86 parts added, taking portfolio to 5,740 parts.

segments.name: Consumer (electronics, toys, durables)
segments.commentary: Revenue INR734 million (+190% YoY, +16% QoQ) at roughly 22-23% capacity utilisation, similar to Q4. EBITDA loss INR361 million, narrowed by INR112 million QoQ; breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27 with utilisation at 40-50%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue growth of about 45-50%, implying roughly INR1,700-1,800 crore; aerospace growth 25-30% and consumer growth 125-150% over FY26.
Operational EBITDA to double vs FY26 in FY27, weighted to the second half; aerospace segment EBITDA margin above 20%.
Consumer EBITDA breakeven targeted by Q4 FY27; consumer utilisation expected to reach 40-50% by Q4.
PAT milestones: PAT breakeven by H1 FY28, consumer PAT breakeven by FY30, decent PAT in FY31 with about 20% steady-state ROCE.
Steady-state EBITDA margin guidance 18-22% (aerospace 18-22%, consumer 18-20%); ROCE target 18-20% steady state.

FY27 capex about INR660 crore (originally INR500 crore consumer, INR160 crore aerospace); aerospace capex may be accelerated. Five-year capex of USD350-400 million over FY27-FY31; about USD150 million equity raise expected, not planned this year unless capex pulled in or inorganic opportunity arises.
capex_capacity: Hosur ecosystem: about INR1,900 crore total investment over 10 years including JVs; first machining facility to commence in H2 FY27 (Sept to March window), with revenue from FY29 and vertical integration largely complete by 2030.
Aerospace capacity being added continuously (about one machine per week); management says aerospace utilisation can comfortably reach 75%.
Management is evaluating accelerating aerospace capex to meet new Farnborough wins; additional INR2,800 crore planned across consumer and aerospace in Karnataka.
Consumer capex (around INR400-500 crore) is for capacity augmentation and new programmes; part of it would not be committed if utilisation ramp fails.
demand_pricing: Farnborough: long-term agreements with two new aerostructure Tier-1 customers and first contract for fully integrated A320 wheels with Safran Landing Systems (single source, about 15-year agreement, contract value not disclosed). New wins not yet in the Q1 order book; expected to reflect next quarter.
Management reports no specific demand change from tariffs or trade policy; customer allocations are being committed.
Consumer demand described as customer-driven; all production is being shipped.
Raw materials about 99% imported; limited qualified Indian sources for super alloys, titanium and aerospace aluminium (only two grades qualified, for forging).
Named consumer customers: Mattel (toys, strategic, scaling up) and Tramontina (consumer durables); a large consumer electronics brand is unnamed.

qa_highlights.question: Size of the A320 wheels contract with Safran Landing Systems, and whether its margin is above the ~20-23% aerospace segment average; is it single-source?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose contract value or margin, calling it the first complete Make-in-India wheel programme and a ~15-year agreement; confirmed it is single-source. It said the margin is 'much larger' but each business delivers the right returns.

qa_highlights.question: Consumer utilisation fell from ~23% in Q4 to ~22% in Q1 while revenue rose; was there capacity addition, and is Q4 EBITDA breakeven still on track?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no capacity was added; the drop reflects better asset utilisation and yield, with revenue up 16% QoQ at similar utilisation. It remains on track for Q4 FY27 consumer EBITDA breakeven and expects 40-50% utilisation by Q4.

qa_highlights.question: Why is depreciation high, how does the FY27 revenue guidance compare with Q1 run-rate, and what is the outlook for other income?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation stays around INR455 million per quarter because capitalisation stopped at end-Q3 FY26 and Q4 was the first full quarter of consumer depreciation; it rises only with more capex. Full-year 45-50% growth relies on higher Q4 consumer revenue at 40-50% utilisation. Other income is interest plus FX; FX is not projected, and interest income should stay near Q1 levels.

qa_highlights.question: Asset turns and steady-state ROCE on new investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer asset turns are about 1.5x and stable; steady-state ROCE is 18-20%, similar to aerospace. ROCE targets are used when allocating capital.

qa_highlights.question: Impact of tariffs and trade policy on localisation or sourcing shifts; is consumer demand structural or restocking?
qa_highlights.answer: Management sees no specific change from tariffs; customers are committing supplier allocations. Consumer demand is customer-driven, and all production is being shipped.

qa_highlights.question: Capex split for FY27 (INR660 crore) and whether consumer capex depends on utilisation ramp; Hosur investment and timing.
qa_highlights.answer: FY27 capex was originally INR500 crore consumer and INR160 crore aerospace, and aerospace may be accelerated with savings in consumer. Consumer capex (INR400-500 crore) would be partly deferred if the utilisation ramp fails. Hosur is about INR1,900 crore over 10 years including JVs, with the first machining facility in H2 FY27 and revenue from FY29.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses roughly double YoY, and will the cost base rise?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer electronics costs were capitalised in Q1 FY26 and expensed from Q4 FY26. Costs have a variable part that grows with revenue and a fixed part that stays flat in the near term. The fixed/variable split was not disclosed.

risks_watch: Consumer utilisation: reported at about 22% in Q1 (vs ~23% in Q4); the Q4 FY27 EBITDA breakeven depends on reaching 40-50%.
Other income dependence: reported EBITDA fell because other income dropped from INR279 million to INR67 million; FX gains are not projected.
Funding: about USD150 million equity raise is expected but not planned this year unless capex is pulled forward or an inorganic deal arises; FY27 capex may be accelerated for aerospace.
Order book conversion: Farnborough wins are not in the Q1 USD1,004 million order book and are expected to reflect next quarter; contract values were not disclosed.
Raw material import dependence (~99% imported) and limited qualified Indian sources for super alloys, titanium and aerospace aluminium (two grades qualified, for forging).
CFO transition: Dinesh Iyer stepped down at end-June 2026; interim finance led by Harish Bang, full-time search ongoing.
Depreciation stays around INR455 million per quarter, and PAT loss of INR532 million continues until PAT breakeven targeted by H1 FY28.
key_quotes: Our consumer segment EBITDA loss narrowed by INR112 million sequentially.
That operational trajectory, not the currency line, is the measure of execution and it's moving exactly as we committed.
We are not disclosing that contract value.
We are not planning to do anything this year unless there is advanced pull-in of capex or inorganic piece, you know.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the aerospace order book, Farnborough wins and the Q4 FY27 consumer breakeven target. Cautious and evasive on specifics: contract value and margin for the A320 wheels, consumer segment split between electronics and toys, FY28+ PAT margin, and the fixed/variable cost split were all withheld or deferred.
